title: Daily Market Digest: November 5, 2026
subtitle: Wall Street Reverses Course as AI Stocks Plummet

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Plunge, Reversing Wednesday's Gains Amid AI Sell-off
items.summary: U.S. stock markets experienced a significant downturn on Thursday, November 5, with major indices closing sharply lower. The sell-off was predominantly driven by a steep decline in AI and chip-related stocks, as investors weighed the implications of Democratic victories in the U.S. midterm elections and concerns over potential slowdowns in data center infrastructure development. This reversal erased the previous day's broad rally.

items.statContext: Fell 212.50 points to 7,476.12 amid broad market decline.
Dropped over 1,000 points, closing at 24,717.03, entering correction territory.

items.headline: Veracyte Plummets on Guidance Cut
items.summary: Veracyte, Inc. shares collapsed after the company lowered its 2026 testing revenue forecast.

items.headline: AMD Shares Decline Amid AI Sector Sell-off
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices experienced a significant drop as investors pulled out of AI-related chip stocks.

items.headline: Tesla Shares Drop
items.summary: Tesla's stock saw a notable decline during today's trading session.

items.headline: Nvidia Shares Continue Decline
items.summary: Nvidia, a key AI chipmaker, continued its downward trend as the AI sector faced intense selling pressure.

items.summary: AppLovin Corp. stood out as a significant gainer today.

items.headline: Sunrun Rallies on Earnings Beat

items.headline: AI and Chip Stocks Lead Market Downturn on Regulatory Fears
items.summary: A broad sell-off in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks drove Wall Street lower today. Investors are expressing concerns that the Democratic party's sweeping victories in the U.S. midterm elections could lead to a slowdown in the development of AI data centers due to potential increased regulation. This fear of a slower data center buildout directly impacted chipmakers and data-center suppliers.

items.headline: Rotation into Defensive Sectors as Tech Slides
items.summary: As the technology sector experienced a sharp decline, investors rotated into more defensive sectors. Shares of consumer staples, healthcare, and utility companies showed gains amidst the broader market weakness.

items.headline: U.S. Census Bureau Releases New Business Trends Data
items.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau today released new data products from its Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS). This survey provides ongoing measurements of business conditions and projections, offering insights into the state of the U.S. economy, excluding farms.

items.headline: Southern Company and Trulieve Cannabis Report Q3 Earnings
items.summary: Southern Company reported third-quarter earnings of $2.0 billion, or $1.77 per share, an increase from the prior year. Operating revenues rose 13.0%. Trulieve Cannabis Corp. also announced Q3 2026 results, with revenue of $230 million and a gross margin of 64%, achieving a positive net income.

items.headline: Key Companies Set to Report Earnings After Market Close
items.summary: Several major companies, including SoundHound AI ($SOUN), IonQ ($IONQ), Airbnb ($ABNB), DraftKings ($DKNG), Devon Energy ($DVN), EOG Resources ($EOG), and Affirm ($AFRM) are scheduled to release their earnings reports after the market closes today.
